_readme: `surfaceMarkers` are the literal strings a human READ in the resolved package on the
date below. They are quoted, not inferred: the defect this guard closes is a sentence
about a dependency that nobody re-read for a year.
`stalePatterns` are stored as regex SOURCE strings so this file does not match the
pattern it declares (`not\s+fully\s+lockable` as literal text contains backslash-s,
This declaration asserts a CAPABILITY IN AN ARTIFACT. It asserts nothing about whether
the operator's E2B tier honours a network body at runtime — that is unmeasured, and a
probe is a separate unit. Do not read this file as 'egress is locked'.

surfaceMarkers.why: the egress option type exists at all: allowOut / denyOut / rules / allowPublicTraffic
SandboxOpts — i.e. Sandbox.create's own options — carries it
SandboxInfo carries it back, so an applied configuration is READABLE (the read-back that makes a tolerant or self-hosted 200 detectable)
a RUNNING sandbox's egress configuration can be replaced
the runtime actually serialises the option rather than declaring a type nothing sends
and puts the result in the POST /sandboxes body
the update endpoint is real, not a type-only stub
getInfo maps the server's response back, which is what a read-back verification would consume

stalePatterns.why: The sentence family that actually occurred, in six tracked files, for a year: 'Managed-E2B egress is not fully lockable' (REFUTED as a capability claim — E8-F007). It is a NEGATIVE CAPABILITY CLAIM about a dependency, and the installed dependency contradicts it (surfaceMarkers above). Quoting it stays legal — the record has to be able to quote what it corrects — but only with a correctionMarker within contextWindowLines. This pattern covers the sentence, NOT the idea: a rewording evades it, and saying so is cheaper than letting a reader believe the class is covered.
